extraction.name: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts, covering 9.6K human-written questions and 23.1K machine-generated questions, focusing on visual and logical reasoning.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.10244.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Machine-generated QA pairs were produced by fine-tuning T5 on SQuAD and applying to human-written chart summaries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chart images and underlying data tables from Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For machine-generated questions, invalid questions were filtered out if the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to provide two questions per chart (compositional and visual) and answers. Each question was answered by two workers; if answers matched exactly, it was considered correct; otherwise, manually checked. Machine-generated QA: T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD generated questions from chart summaries; answers were extracted from summaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%; after considering typos and lexical variations, agreement on 500 random samples was 78.55%.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models cannot effectively handle nested operations; performance decreases when gold data table is not provided due to automatic data extraction errors; lower performance on pie charts and visual questions.
